title: Precision: constraints, format and examples
summary: Control length, structure and style, and show the model what good looks like.

lessons.title: Constraints are instructions
lessons.body: Limits on length, tone, sources and things to avoid make answers shorter to edit. 'Under 200 words, plain English, no jargon' beats 'make it good'.

lessons.title: Format and examples
lessons.body: Ask for the shape you need: a table, numbered steps, JSON. One short example of the output style (few-shot) usually beats a paragraph of description.

exercises.title: Constrain the answer
exercises.scenario: You need a 150-word abstract for a lab report.
exercises.task: Write a prompt with clear limits on length, tone and what to leave out.
exercises.model_answer_tip: 'Write a formal 150-word abstract for my chemistry lab report from the notes below. Avoid first person and do not invent results.'

exercises.title: Ask for a structure
exercises.scenario: You want to compare two theories for an essay.
exercises.task: Ask for a comparison in a specific structure.

checks.label: Asks for a table or headings
checks.hint: Ask for a table or headed sections.

exercises.model_answer_tip: 'Compare behaviourism and constructivism in a table with columns for key idea, strengths, weaknesses and one classroom example.'

exercises.title: Show, do not tell
exercises.scenario: You want feedback written in a consistent style.
exercises.task: Include one short example of the feedback style you want.

checks.label: Includes an example marker
checks.hint: Add an 'Example:' with a short sample.

checks.label: Long enough to hold an example

exercises.model_answer_tip: 'Give feedback on my paragraph in this style. Example: Strength: clear claim. Fix: add evidence from week 3. Next step: cite one source.'
